pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/fixture.ts:19 The ServerBoard seam keeps a second adapter (fixture.ts, 374 lines, plus fixtureData.ts) that re-implements the kernel's decision rules but that no route, test or contract suite runs, so it can drift from the real side with nothing noticing; seams-and-adapters says to check every double against the shared contract or stop paying for it.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/port.ts:35 The enabling point is a hard-coded constant, so the fixture adapter is never substituted at run time, and per port.ts:9-11 no test imports it. The seam itself does hold: real.ts:64 takes a test adapter and board-keepalive.test.ts drives a stand-in board. The defect is the unchecked, unreached double.

app/(studio)/board/_board/Board.tsx:9 The island hands optimistic state, debouncing and the history to the gate kernel and the port. The desk learns a small interface and gets the whole decision lifecycle.

app/(studio)/board/_port/keepalive.ts:17 The flush logic takes a plain context (who, input, params) rather than a Next request. The route at [packet]/keepalive/route.ts:24 is a one-line shim, so a test drives the body over a stand-in board.
app/(studio)/board/_board/load.ts:4 First paint and every later write go through one serverBoard() port, so a change to how packets are read lands in one place.
